column1: samuel:anoints-kings|1 Samuel 10:1;1 Samuel 16:13|Prophets|intermediate|Which prophet anointed both Saul and David as king?|Samuel;Nathan;Gad;Ahijah|Samuel poured oil on Saul and later anointed David among his brothers. Both anointing accounts explicitly name him.

nathan:ewe-lamb|2 Samuel 12:1-7|Prophets|intermediate|Which prophet confronted David with the story of a rich man taking a poor man's ewe lamb?|Nathan;Gad;Samuel;Ahijah|Nathan told the parable and then identified David as the man. The question concerns this rebuke after the Uriah and Bathsheba episode.

elisha:naaman|2 Kings 5:8-14|Prophets|intermediate|Which prophet sent Naaman instructions to wash seven times in the Jordan?|Elisha;Elijah;Micaiah;Ahijah|Elisha sent the washing instructions through a messenger. The revised wording distinguishes his instruction from physically washing Naaman himself.

hezekiah:isaiah-sennacherib|2 Kings 19:1-7;2 Kings 20:5-6|Kings and succession|advanced|Which king received Isaiah's assurance during the Assyrian threat and a promise of fifteen added years?|Hezekiah;Ahaz;Manasseh;Josiah|The two passages identify Hezekiah. They connect Isaiah's counsel about Assyria with the later promise concerning the king's life.

josiah:book-of-law|2 Kings 22:1,8-11|Kings and succession|intermediate|Which king began reigning at eight and heard the law book found during temple repairs?|Josiah;Joash;Manasseh;Amon|Josiah began at eight. The same chapter records Hilkiah's discovery and Shaphan's reading to him; Joash was another child king but does not fit these details.

isaiah:call-uzziah|Isaiah 6:1|Prophets|intermediate|In the year of which king's death did Isaiah see the Lord seated on a high throne?|Uzziah;Jotham;Ahaz;Hezekiah|Isaiah dates this vision to the year King Uzziah died. The alternatives were other kings of Judah, but not the one named in the date.

jehoiakim:scroll|Jeremiah 36:9,21-23|Kings and succession|advanced|Which king cut Jeremiah's scroll with a penknife and burned it as Jehudi read it?|Jehoiakim;Josiah;Jehoiachin;Zedekiah|The chapter identifies Jehoiakim as the king who destroyed the scroll. Jehudi read it; he was not the ruler ordering its destruction.

uzziah:leprosy|2 Chronicles 26:1,16-21|Priesthood|advanced|Which king was struck with leprosy after entering the temple to burn incense despite the priests' warning?|Uzziah;Jotham;Ahaz;Hezekiah|Uzziah attempted a priestly duty and was struck with leprosy while angry with the priests. His son Jotham then handled royal affairs.

jehu:anointed|2 Kings 9:1-6|Kings and succession|advanced|Which commander was called out from his fellow officers at Ramoth-gilead and anointed king by Elisha's messenger?|Jehu;Hazael;Zimri;Omri|The messenger sought Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi and privately anointed him. This corrects the original reference's overbroad claim about later actions.

deborah:palm-tree|Judges 4:4-5|Judges|intermediate|Which prophetess judged Israel under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel?|Deborah;Huldah;Miriam;Noadiah|Judges identifies Deborah, wife of Lappidoth, as the prophetess and judge at this location.

gideon:three-hundred|Judges 7:2-7|Wars and battles|intermediate|Whose army was reduced first by sending the fearful home and then by a drinking test to three hundred men?|Gideon's;Barak's;Jephthah's;Saul's|The instructions and tests were given to Gideon. The purpose of reducing the army is explained in the same account.

abiathar:nob|1 Samuel 22:20-23|Priesthood|advanced|Which son of Ahimelech escaped the killing of the priests and fled to David?|Abiathar;Zadok;Hilkiah;Jehoiada|Abiathar escaped and reported the deaths to David. Ahimelech was his father; the alternatives are distinct priests.

jehoiada:joash|2 Kings 11:4-16|Priesthood|advanced|Which priest organised the guards and the coronation of Joash that ended Athaliah's rule?|Jehoiada;Abiathar;Zadok;Hilkiah|Jehoiada made the arrangements, brought out the king's son and directed the guards. Athaliah's killing was carried out under his orders outside the temple.

caiaphas:trial|Matthew 26:57-65|Priesthood|advanced|Which high priest tore his garments during Jesus' hearing in Matthew 26?|Caiaphas;Annas;Ananias;Abiathar|Matthew locates the assembly at Caiaphas's house and identifies the high priest's action. The other priests belong to different hearings or periods.

huldah:book-of-law|2 Kings 22:14-20|Prophets|intermediate|Which prophetess did Josiah's officials consult after finding the Book of the Law?|Huldah;Deborah;Miriam;Noadiah|The officials went to Huldah, wife of Shallum. She delivered the answer to the king; Hilkiah's discovery and Shaphan's reading are separate roles.

ruth:boaz-david|Ruth 4:13-17|Genealogy|intermediate|Which Moabite woman became the mother of Obed, the father of Jesse?|Ruth;Naomi;Orpah;Tamar|Ruth bore Obed after marrying Boaz. Naomi helped care for him, but the text does not identify her as his biological mother.

rahab:jericho-matthew-hebrews|Joshua 2:1-4;Matthew 1:5;Hebrews 11:31|Scriptural connections|mastery|Which woman sheltered spies at Jericho, appears as Boaz's mother in Matthew, and is named in Hebrews' examples of faith?|Rahab;Ruth;Tamar;Bathsheba|The three references identify Rahab in the specified roles. The other women appear in the genealogy but do not satisfy the Jericho and Hebrews clues.

thomas:absent|John 20:24-28|Gospels|beginner|Which apostle was absent at the earlier appearance and later addressed Jesus as his Lord and God?|Thomas;Peter;Andrew;Philip|John names Thomas, called Didymus, as the absent disciple and later speaker. The wording is paraphrased rather than offered as an exact quotation.

boaz:david-relation|Ruth 4:21-22|Genealogy|intermediate|In Ruth's recorded line Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David, what relationship does Boaz have to David?|Great-grandfather;Grandfather;Father;Uncle|The written line places Obed and Jesse between Boaz and David. It therefore records three parent-to-child links.

samuel:obey-sacrifice|1 Samuel 15:20-23|Prophets|intermediate|Who told Saul that obedience was better than sacrifice after the sparing of Agag and the livestock?|Samuel;Nathan;Gad;Ahijah|Samuel answered Saul's defence by contrasting obedience with sacrifice. He was addressing the king, not reporting words spoken by Saul.

ruth:whither-thou-goest|Ruth 1:16-17|Family and customs|intermediate|Who pledged to go where another went and accept her people and God in Ruth 1?|Ruth to Naomi;Naomi to Ruth;Orpah to Naomi;Ruth to Boaz|Ruth addressed Naomi with the pledge. Orpah had departed, and Boaz does not participate in this conversation.

ahasuerus:jewish-defense|Esther 8:7-11|Exile and restoration|advanced|Under whose authority did Esther and Mordecai issue the decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves?|Ahasuerus's;Cyrus's;Darius's;Artaxerxes'|The king authorised writing in his name and sealing with his ring. This preserves the distinction between royal authority and the people who prepared the decree.

nebuchadnezzar:jehoiachin|2 Kings 24:10-17|Exile and restoration|advanced|Which king took Jehoiachin captive and installed his uncle Mattaniah, renaming him Zedekiah?|Nebuchadnezzar;Sennacherib;Shalmaneser;Esarhaddon|The account names Nebuchadnezzar as Babylon's king and describes the captivity and installation. The other rulers were Assyrian.

ezra:reads-law|Nehemiah 8:1-3|Exile and restoration|intermediate|Who brought the law book before the assembly and read it from early morning until midday?|Ezra;Nehemiah;Zerubbabel;Jeshua|Ezra the priest and scribe brought and read the law. The other leaders had different roles in the restoration narratives.

markfam|Acts 12:25|Early church|advanced|Whom did Barnabas and Saul take with them after completing their relief service, according to Acts 12:25?|John Mark;Silas;Timothy;Judas Barsabbas|The verse names John whose surname was Mark. The wording avoids making the question depend on a disputed direction of travel in textual variants.

adonijah|1 Kings 1:5-10|Kings and succession|advanced|Which son of David sought the throne with Joab and Abiathar supporting him?|Adonijah;Absalom;Amnon;Chileab|Adonijah said that he would be king and conferred with Joab and Abiathar. Absalom's earlier rebellion had a different political setting.

herod|Acts 12:1-4;Matthew 2:1;Luke 3:1;Acts 25:13|Same-name identities|mastery|Which Herod is the king in Acts 12 who killed James and imprisoned Peter?|Herod Agrippa I;Herod the Great;Herod Antipas;Herod Agrippa II|Acts 12 calls him Herod the king. The Agrippa I identification distinguishes him from the birth-narrative king, the tetrarch of Galilee and the later Agrippa who heard Paul; the full historical identification needs a historical source beyond these verses.

mephi|2 Samuel 9:1-13|Same-name identities|advanced|Which member of Saul's house was lame in both feet and ate at David's table for Jonathan's sake?|Mephibosheth son of Jonathan;Ish-bosheth son of Saul;Mica son of Mephibosheth;Mephibosheth son of Saul|The narrative identifies Jonathan's son and names his own son Mica. Saul also had a son called Mephibosheth, so the father's name is important.

flight|1 Samuel 21:1,10;1 Samuel 22:1;1 Samuel 23:5|Chronology|mastery|In Samuel's narrative, which sequence correctly orders these places in David's flight and campaigns?|Nob, Gath, Adullam, Keilah;Gath, Nob, Adullam, Keilah;Nob, Adullam, Gath, Keilah;Adullam, Nob, Gath, Keilah|The cited scenes place David at Nob, then Gath, then the cave of Adullam, and later at Keilah. This is the order of selected stops, not a claim that there were no intervening locations.

carmel|1 Kings 18:40-42|Chronology|advanced|Immediately after the killing of Baal's prophets at Kishon, what did Elijah tell Ahab to do?|Go up, eat and drink;Go down, cross the Jordan;Go home, hide from Jezebel;Go out, seek Elisha|Elijah told Ahab to eat and drink because there was the sound of abundant rain. The later flight from Jezebel belongs to another episode.

thess|Acts 17:1|Geography|advanced|Which two cities did Paul and Silas pass through before reaching Thessalonica in Acts 17?|Amphipolis and Apollonia;Neapolis and Amphipolis;Apollonia and Berea;Amphipolis and Berea|Acts names Amphipolis and Apollonia in that order before Thessalonica. Berea appears after Thessalonica in the narrative.

satan-census|1 Chronicles 21:1;2 Samuel 24:1|Textual nuance|mastery|Which account names Satan as provoking David to number Israel, whereas the parallel opens with Jehovah's anger?|1 Chronicles;2 Samuel;1 Kings;2 Chronicles|First Chronicles names Satan; the parallel in 2 Samuel introduces the action through Jehovah's anger. The question preserves the difference without asserting a harmonisation.

elah|1 Samuel 17:2|Geography|beginner|In which valley were Saul's forces arrayed against the Philistines when David faced Goliath?|Elah;Jezreel;Achor;Rephaim|First Samuel places the opposing armies in the valley of Elah. The alternatives are other biblical valleys, not this encounter's location.

azotus|Acts 8:39-40|Geography|intermediate|Where was Philip found after the Ethiopian official's baptism?|Azotus;Joppa;Lydda;Caesarea|Philip was found at Azotus and continued preaching through the cities until Caesarea. Caesarea was the later endpoint, not where he was first found.

matthias|Acts 1:23-26|Early church|beginner|Who was numbered with the eleven apostles after the lot was cast between him and Joseph Barsabbas?|Matthias;Barnabas;Silas;Cleopas|The lot fell on Matthias. Joseph called Barsabbas was the other proposed candidate.

house-prayer|Matthew 21:13;Isaiah 56:7;Jeremiah 7:11|Scriptural connections|mastery|Which prophet supplies the house-of-prayer part of Jesus' saying during the temple cleansing, rather than the den-of-robbers part?|Isaiah;Jeremiah;Malachi;Zechariah|The house-of-prayer wording is in Isaiah 56:7; Jeremiah 7:11 supplies the den-of-robbers image. The saying combines two sources, so either prophet cannot answer both clauses indiscriminately.

felix:paul-prison|Acts 24:27|Offices and roles|advanced|Which governor left Paul imprisoned when Porcius Festus succeeded him?|Felix;Gallio;Pilate;Sergius Paulus|Acts identifies Felix as the departing governor and explains that he wished to gain favour with the Jews. Festus was his successor.

gallio:corinth|Acts 18:12-17|Offices and roles|advanced|Which proconsul refused to judge the religious charges brought against Paul at Corinth?|Gallio;Sergius Paulus;Felix;Festus|Gallio dismissed the dispute as concerning words, names and the opponents' law. Sergius Paulus was a different proconsul; Felix and Festus handled later hearings.

silas:philippi|Acts 16:19-25|Early church|intermediate|Who was imprisoned with Paul at Philippi after the incident with the slave girl?|Silas;Barnabas;Timothy;John Mark|The narrative names Paul and Silas as the men dragged before the magistrates, beaten and imprisoned.

titus:crete|Titus 1:5|Early church|intermediate|Whom had Paul left in Crete to put matters in order and appoint elders?|Titus;Timothy;Tychicus;Epaphras|The letter addresses Titus and explains why he was left in Crete. Timothy's assignment at Ephesus is a different instruction.

timothy:circumcised|Acts 16:1-3|Early church|intermediate|Which disciple, whose mother was Jewish and father Greek, did Paul circumcise before taking him along?|Timothy;Titus;Silas;Apollos|Acts names Timothy and gives the local circumstances. This should not be confused with Paul's account of Titus, who was not compelled to be circumcised.

ananias:damascus|Acts 9:10-18|Same-name identities|advanced|Who was instructed in a vision to visit Saul at Judas's house on Straight Street?|Ananias the Damascus disciple;Ananias the high priest;Ananias the husband of Sapphira;Annas the high priest|The passage introduces a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The name and role distinguish him from the other Ananias figures and from Annas.

isaiah:voice-john|Matthew 3:3;Isaiah 40:3|Scriptural connections|advanced|Which prophet supplies Matthew's voice-in-the-wilderness passage applied to John the Baptist?|Isaiah;Jeremiah;Malachi;Micah|Matthew names Isaiah, and Isaiah 40:3 contains the wilderness and highway imagery. Other messenger passages should not be substituted for this quotation.

micah:bethlehem|Matthew 2:4-6;Micah 5:2|Scriptural connections|advanced|Which prophetic book contains the Bethlehem ruler passage cited in Matthew's account of Herod's inquiry?|Micah;Isaiah;Jeremiah;Hosea|Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem and the coming ruler. Matthew's chapter also uses Hosea and Jeremiah for different parts of its narrative.

jonah:sign|Matthew 12:39-40;Jonah 1:17|Scriptural connections|intermediate|Whose time in the great fish did Jesus compare with the Son of man's time in the heart of the earth?|Jonah's;Noah's;Elijah's;Moses'|Jesus explicitly refers to Jonah's three days and nights. The other figures' deliverances are not the sign named here.

david:throne-promise|Luke 1:32-33;2 Samuel 7:12-16|Scriptural connections|advanced|Whose throne did Gabriel say Mary's son would receive, echoing the enduring kingdom promise in 2 Samuel 7?|David's;Solomon's;Saul's;Hezekiah's|Gabriel explicitly names David's throne. The promise spoken to David in Samuel concerns the endurance of his house and kingdom.

jehu:not-judah|2 Kings 9:1-3|Kings and succession|intermediate|Over which kingdom did Elisha's messenger anoint Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi?|Israel;Judah;Aram;Moab|The anointing instruction names Israel. This positive formulation replaces an overbroad negative item and clarifies Jehu's immediate father and grandfather.

judah-early-kings:order|1 Kings 11:43;1 Kings 14:31;1 Kings 15:8|Chronology|advanced|Which sequence follows the recorded succession from Solomon through Asa?|Solomon, Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa;Solomon, Rehoboam, Asa, Abijah;Rehoboam, Solomon, Abijah, Asa;Solomon, Abijah, Rehoboam, Asa|The succession notices link Solomon to Rehoboam, Rehoboam to Abijam (Abijah), and Abijam to Asa. All alternatives use the same rulers.

judah-middle-kings:order|2 Kings 20:21;2 Kings 21:18,26|Chronology|advanced|Which sequence follows the succession from Hezekiah through Josiah?|Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, Josiah;Hezekiah, Amon, Manasseh, Josiah;Manasseh, Hezekiah, Amon, Josiah;Hezekiah, Manasseh, Josiah, Amon|The notices identify each successor: Manasseh after Hezekiah, Amon after Manasseh and Josiah after Amon. The alternatives reverse those links.

amos|Amos 7:10-14|Prophets|advanced|Which prophet did Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, tell to flee to Judah?|Amos;Hosea;Jonah;Micah|Amaziah spoke to Amos after reporting his words to Jeroboam. The revised stem distinguishes Amaziah's allegation from the prophet's own exact words.

judas|John 14:22|Same-name identities|advanced|How does John 14:22 distinguish the Judas who asked about Jesus manifesting himself to the disciples?|Judas, not Iscariot;Judas, called Barsabbas;Judas, the Galilean;Judas, of Straight Street|John identifies the speaker as Judas, not Iscariot. The wording avoids forcing a disputed cross-list family identification into the question.

hosea|Matthew 2:15;Hosea 11:1|Scriptural connections|mastery|Which prophet supplies Matthew's statement about calling a son out of Egypt, originally referring to Israel?|Hosea;Jeremiah;Isaiah;Micah|Hosea explicitly names Israel before the statement. Matthew applies the statement to Jesus; Micah and Jeremiah supply other passages in Matthew 2.

sheba|Matthew 12:42;1 Kings 10:1-3|Scriptural connections|advanced|Which royal visitor's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom underlies Jesus' reference to the queen of the south?|The queen of Sheba;The queen of Persia;The queen of Judah;The queen of Israel|Kings records the queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon. Jesus invokes the queen of the south's journey to hear that wisdom, not an episode about another queen.

overlap|Isaiah 1:1;Micah 1:1;Hosea 1:1;Jeremiah 1:2-3|Textual nuance|mastery|Which prophet's opening dates his ministry from Josiah's reign, unlike the other three openings that explicitly name Hezekiah?|Jeremiah;Isaiah;Micah;Hosea|Jeremiah's opening names Josiah's thirteenth year; the other three openings include Hezekiah. This tests explicit headings, not a speculative claim about who could have met.

jehoiada|2 Chronicles 24:15-22|Textual nuance|mastery|Which statement distinguishes Jehoiada's end from that of his son Zechariah in 2 Chronicles 24?|Jehoiada died aged 130, and Zechariah was stoned at Joash's command;Zechariah died aged 130, and Jehoiada was stoned at Joash's command;Both were stoned at Joash's command after rebuking him;Both died aged 130 and were buried among the kings|The narrative records Jehoiada's old age, death and royal burial before describing the killing of his son. The original negative question is replaced by a direct account comparison.

obadiah|1 Kings 18:3-7|Obscure people|advanced|Who both managed Ahab's household and sheltered a hundred prophets from Jezebel?|Obadiah;Micaiah;Jehu son of Hanani;Zedekiah son of Chenaanah|Kings explicitly gives Obadiah both roles. His household position does not identify him with the author of the book of Obadiah.

conclusion|Ruth 4:22;1 Kings 1:32-34;1 Kings 11:43|Genealogy|mastery|In the recorded line Jesse, David, Solomon, Rehoboam, how many parent-to-child links separate Jesse from Rehoboam?|Three;Two;Four;Five|The sequence has three links. It tests the stated family chain without replacing one figure with an uncle or assuming extra chronological information.

elisha-wrong|1 Kings 18:36-38;2 Kings 4:1-7;2 Kings 5:10-14;2 Kings 6:5-7|Scriptural connections|mastery|Which event belongs to Elijah's ministry rather than Elisha's in the cited narratives?|Fire consuming the offering on Mount Carmel;A borrowed iron axe head floating;Naaman washing in the Jordan;A widow filling borrowed vessels with oil|Kings names Elijah at the Carmel offering. The other three episodes are in the Elisha narratives, with his role varying between instruction and action.

zimri|2 Kings 9:30-31|Textual nuance|advanced|Who invoked Zimri's killing of his master while addressing Jehu from a window at Jezreel?|Jezebel;Athaliah;Huldah;Abigail|The speaker is Jezebel. The saying is hers, and must not be confused with the narrator asserting that Jehu and Zimri had identical careers.

jonah-nineveh|2 Kings 14:23-25;Jonah 1:1-2|Scriptural connections|mastery|Which prophet is linked with Jeroboam son of Joash in Kings and commissioned to go to Nineveh in his own book?|Jonah son of Amittai;Nahum the Elkoshite;Amos of Tekoa;Hosea son of Beeri|Both passages identify Jonah son of Amittai. Nahum also has an oracle concerning Nineveh but is not the prophet named in the Kings passage.

trio|2 Kings 19:1-7|Scriptural connections|advanced|Which king and prophet were involved in the response to the Assyrian threat in 2 Kings 19?|Hezekiah and Isaiah;Josiah and Isaiah;Hezekiah and Jeremiah;Josiah and Jeremiah|Hezekiah sent messengers to Isaiah, who answered the king's fear of the Assyrian threat. The alternatives change one or both participants.

antipas:john-baptist|Matthew 14:1-11|Kings and succession|advanced|Which ruler, called the tetrarch in Matthew 14, ordered John the Baptist beheaded?|Herod;Pontius Pilate;Porcius Festus;Gallio|Matthew identifies Herod the tetrarch and says he sent to have John beheaded. The question retains the title used by the text rather than making the unqualified name Herod identify every ruler of that dynasty.

agrippa2:paul|Acts 25:13-14;Acts 26:1-3|Offices and roles|advanced|Which king arrived with Bernice and then heard Paul's defence after Festus became governor?|Agrippa;Herod of the birth narrative;Archelaus;The emperor Claudius|Acts names King Agrippa arriving with Bernice and giving Paul permission to speak. The setting distinguishes this Agrippa from the Herod of earlier narratives.
